title: Does 1/2-Tsallis-INF Also Work Well for Best-Arm Identification?
abstract: arXiv:2608.15365v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Regret minimization (RM) and best-arm identification (BAI) are two fundamental objectives in multi-armed bandits. Among regret-minimizing algorithms, $1/2$-Tsallis-INF is a canonical best-of-both-worlds FTRL algorithm: it achieves logarithmic pseudo-regret in stochastic bandits while retaining minimax-optimal regret in adversarial bandits, without knowing the environment in advance. This raises a natural question: can the same algorithm, without additional exploration, also identify the best arm reliably? We study this question in stochastic bandits by analyzing the failure probability $\operatorname{Err}_t$, defined as the probability that the empirical best arm determined by the cumulative importance-weighted loss estimates of 1/2-Tsallis-INF differs from the true optimal arm. tldr: 本文研究了 1/2-Tsallis-INF 算法在随机多臂老虎机中是否无需额外探索即可可靠识别最佳臂，并分析了其失败概率，填补了遗憾最小化与最佳臂识别之间的理论空白。
en_tdlr: This paper investigates whether the 1/2-Tsallis-INF algorithm can reliably identify the best arm without extra exploration in stochastic bandits, analyzing its failure probability and bridging regret minimization with best-arm identification.
